article.deck: The Oct. 27 breakout past the 22.38 buy point has stalled; the stock sits 9.0% under it after bouncing off the 50-day line, so the 22.38-23.50 buy range is out of reach for now.
body: SailPoint rose 1.15, or 6.0%, to 20.36, trading 0.9x its 50-day average volume. The stock cleared a five-week cup, 17.8% deep, with a 22.38 buy point on Oct. 27, on 0.65x average volume. Nine sessions later it closes 9.0% below that buy point, a stalled breakout. The cup formed after a bigger correction, and the stock is still under its 24.00 high from Oct. 6, 2025.

Monday's gain came off the 50-day line at 19.95; the close sits 2.0% above it and 1.4% above the 21-day line at 20.08, 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line, so the trend is intact rather than stretched. The 52-week high is 22.62, 10.0% overhead. SailPoint holds an RS rank of 80 of 99 on the desk's list, but its RS line is 14.4% below its high, and the stock is up just 0.6% this year. After hours it traded at 20.49, up 0.6%.

The company is still losing money. In the quarter ended July 31 it lost 9 cents a share on revenue of $308.8 million, up 16.8% from a year earlier. The three quarters before that were losses of 13 cents, 6 cents and 6 cents, on revenue of $280.1 million, $294.6 million and $281.9 million. The next report is due Dec. 15. TIKR reported on Oct. 23 that SailPoint soared 11% as cybersecurity stocks rallied, and Zacks upgraded the stock to buy the same day.
A close back above 22.38 would put the breakout back in play; a close under the 50-day line would undo Monday's bounce.

article.headline: Starbucks Climbs 3.8% Toward Record As Stifel Resumes With Buy Rating
article.deck: The stock closed 1.1% below the 110.61 buy point of a 12-week cup; the buy range runs to 116.14.
body: Starbucks rose 4.03, or 3.8%, to 109.44 on Monday, trading 1.07x its 50-day average volume, after Stifel resumed coverage with a buy rating and a $115 target, according to headlines from Investing.com and GuruFocus. The close left the stock 1.8% below its 52-week high of 111.50.

The business is familiar: Starbucks roasts, markets and sells coffee around the world through company-run and licensed stores, selling drinks, whole beans and ground coffee, food and packaged and ready-to-drink products. It reports in three segments, North America, International and Channel Development, and licenses its name to grocery and foodservice accounts.

The case for the stock is a profit recovery, not sales growth. In the September quarter Starbucks earned 59 cents a share, up 391.7% from a year earlier; the payload carries no revenue figure for that quarter. In the June quarter it earned 91 cents on revenue of $9.32 billion, down 1.4% from a year earlier. Earlier quarters showed 45 cents on $9.53 billion and 26 cents on $9.92 billion. Earnings have risen from 26 cents to 59 cents over the four quarters given while revenue has drifted, so the gains are coming from margins rather than the top line.
The market is paying for that turn. Starbucks carries a market cap of $124.8 billion and trades at 29.4 times forward earnings, against 49.5 times trailing earnings. The next report is due Jan. 27.

On the chart, Starbucks is building a 12-week cup, 21.0% deep, that started Aug. 13 and bottomed at 87.35 on Oct. 8. The buy point is 110.61 and the buy range runs to 116.14; Monday's close sits 1.1% below the buy point. The stock is up 20.6% in a month and trades 10.3% above its 50-day line at 99.18 and 9.2% above its 200-day line at 100.20. It sits 1.15 ATRs from the 21-day line at 102.76, so the run off the low is firm without being stretched.

Starbucks holds an RS rank of 82 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 3.5% below its high. The stock is up 30.0% this year and 33.1% over 12 months. After hours it traded at 109.31, down 0.1%.
The open question on the chart is whether the stock can close through 110.61 in a market the desk still rates as in correction.
article.watch: Watch for a close above the 110.61 buy point, with the 52-week high of 111.50 just above it.

chief.verdict: A 2.3% pop in the S&P 500 and 2.7% in the Nasdaq doesn't undo a correction: the Nasdaq is still 4.5% under its 50-day line and 8.9% off its high, with six distribution days including the -5.52% hit on Nov. 5. The leadership worth owning has moved to slower names: GWW's 15-week flat base, AMGN and AAPL in buy range, and SBUX and ABNB sitting just under their pivots. Meanwhile the growth software names keep failing. SAIL and GTLB have slid back through their buy points and CRWD, TEAM and NOW are on the sell list. The risk still leans down, and any new buy here is a pilot position that needs a follow-through day behind it.
chief.market: With the market in correction and 7 distribution days on the S&P 500 (weighted 6.8) and 6 on the Nasdaq (weighted 7.8), keep exposure light: one or two pilot buys at most and mostly cash until a follow-through day.

picks.why: This is the cleanest chart on the desk: a 15-week flat base, RS rank 88, and a close of 1447.67, just 1.9% past the 1420.01 buy point, so it is still in range. Flat bases that clear in a weak tape are where institutions hide, and industrials leaders GWW and FAST both broke out this week. The risk is the tape itself: in a correction, breakouts fail more often, and a close back under 1420.01 means the base didn't hold.
picks.entry: Buy within range from 1420.01 up to the 1491.01 maximum at a starter size; cut it on a close back below 1420.01.

It has RS rank 82, earnings up 404.0% year over year by the desk's count, and no report until 2027-01-27, so there is no earnings gamble in the hold. The risk is that it ran 20.6% in a month and sits 10.3% above its 50-day, so it arrives at the pivot tired. Its handle-high early entry at 96.83 is long gone.
